title: PV Labs to receive investment from Lockheed Martin to advance next-generation Apache pilot night vision sensor
summary: The approved investment framework is aligned to Canada’s procurement of 26 Lockheed Martin High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems.
body_markdown:
PV Labs is pleased to announce it has been approved for funding under Canada’s Industrial and Technological Benefits (ITB) Policy and Investment Framework, enabling a strategic investment by Lockheed Martin to support the development of a next-generation Pilot Night Vision Sensor (PNVS) for the Boeing AH-64E Apache helicopter.


The approved investment framework, aligned to Canada’s procurement of 26 Lockheed Martin High Mobility Artillery Rocket Systems (HIMARS), establishes a multi-year roadmap to design and develop an advanced staring-array PNVS designed to enhance Apache helicopter operations in adverse weather, degraded visual environments, and nighttime conditions.


The initiative represents a significant opportunity to contribute to advanced defence sensor development and manufacturing capabilities in Canada while supporting a critical capability for one of the world’s most widely deployed military helicopter platforms.


As a Canadian small and medium-sized business (SMB), PV Labs has built a strong track record of enabling international aerospace and defence original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) to enhance their capabilities through the integration of Canadian innovation and content.


Through applied research and development, technology trade studies, prototype development, and support for domestic manufacturing transitions, PV Labs contributes significantly to Canada’s innovation ecosystem, intellectual property creation, and defence industrial base growth.


“At a time when aerospace and defence sectors are seeing unprecedented momentum, Ontario companies are developing the innovative technologies needed to strengthen global supply chains and drive economic growth at home,” said Vic Fedeli, Ontario’s minister of economic development, job creation and trade.


“Through this partnership with Lockheed Martin, PV Labs will enhance the Apache helicopter with next-generation night-vision sensors, showcasing Ontario-made innovation at a new scale. We congratulate the PV Labs team on this incredible accomplishment and look forward to seeing this project further enhance Ontario’s industrial capacity.”


Leveraging decades of expertise in optronics technologies, airborne ISR systems, and successful execution of ITB-driven programs, PV Labs is uniquely positioned to support the design, prototyping, qualification, and production readiness of a next-generation sensor system.


“This investment framework approval represents a significant milestone for PV Labs and underscores the strength and maturity of Canadian innovation within the global aerospace and defence industry, including its potential integration on one of the world’s most trusted and capable rotary-wing platforms, the Apache helicopter,” said Mark Chamberlain, president and founder, PV Labs.


“It reflects the confidence placed in PV Labs as a low-risk, high-performance technology partner and reinforces our position as Lockheed Martin’s trusted R&D and delivery partner of choice in Canada for complex, advanced optronics systems. Working alongside Lockheed Martin and supported by Canada’s ITB Policy, we have the opportunity to develop a world-class pilotage sensor capability while strengthening Canada’s advanced defence technology and manufacturing base.”


“With over 85 years of presence and partnership in Canada, we are dedicated to strengthening a Canadian defence industry that drives meaningful economic impact,” said Kristen Leroux, vice-president and regional executive for Canada and Latin America at Lockheed Martin.


“This investment champion’s PV Labs’ growth and manufacturing capabilities, advancing opportunities for Canadian industry access to global supply chains.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by PV Labs.*
